Hero.description: A portable, standalone Windows application delivering a refined web interface for yt-dlp. Enables granular stream discovery, audio/video downloading, and rapid media extraction through a seamless WebView2 desktop bridge.

Step1.title: Media Link Extraction & Discovery
Step1.description: Clean obsidian style container UI with dual-language toggle (EN / RU). Queries the CLI daemon asynchronously to populate stream catalogs without blocking the main render thread.

Step2.title: Format & Codec Selection Matrix
Step2.description: Direct inspectability of internal yt-dlp resolutions, framerates, and encoding formats before launching downloads.

Architecture.title: 3-Tier Architecture
Architecture.description: A separation of concerns combining web fluidity, native runtime management, and low-level CLI execution.

Layer1.title: Modern Web UI
Layer1.description: User-facing viewport delivering a reactive state engine, multi-language localization (EN/RU), format picker matrices, and download features.

Layer2.title: .NET Core Middleware
Layer2.description: The bridge backbone. Validates user input, spawns sandboxed CLI child processes, stream-parses stdout/stderr, and sanitizes result file.

Layer3.title: Desktop Shell Host
Layer3.description: Lightweight, single-file Windows executable packaging WebView2 evergreen runtime, with frontend and integrated server orchestration.

Core.title: Underlying Engine: yt-dlp Core
Core.description: Harnesses yt-dlp's massive parser ecosystem with over 1,800+ supported video, audio, and broadcast endpoints worldwide.

Hero.description: A resilient, decentralized digital gaming deals aggregation platform built on an event-driven microservices architecture. Continuously scrapes, normalizes, and compares pricing data across digital distribution platforms like Steam and InstantGaming (with extensible provider adapters for future storefronts).

Workflow.title: Interface in Action — Frontend & Catalog Explorer
Workflow.description: Polished client screens built with Next.js and Tailwind CSS delivering instantaneous search, provider price comparisons, and secured authentication.

Step1.title: Authentication & Secure Access
Step1.description: JWT-powered authentication flow connecting securely to the dedicated Identity Server. Provides cryptographically signed credentials, token refresh, and zero exposure of underlying persistent identity databases.

Step2.title: Multi-Source Price Aggregation Matrix
Step2.description: Comparative game catalog parsing Steam, InstantGaming, and future sources with search, sorting, and pricing overview providing.

Architecture.title: Distributed System Architecture — Event-Driven Microservices
Architecture.description: A modular, decoupled architecture isolating client interaction, task scheduling, asynchronous web scraping, and data storage.

S1.title: Identity Server
S1.description: Dedicated service generating, signing, and refreshing secure JWTs. Manages credentials in an isolated relational database. Reusable across future ecosystem microservices.
S1.type: ASP.NET Core / EF Core / MS SQL

S2.title: Frontend Client
S2.description: User-facing responsive interface communicating via REST with JWT. Delivers game catalog browsing, search filters, and instant deal discovery without direct DB access.

S3.title: Orchestrator Backend
S3.description: The central controller and data guard. Generates scraping tasks, validates inbound JWTs, collects worker results from Redis, and coordinates updates to the core database.

S4.title: Task Broker
S4.description: High-throughput message broker dispatching scraping tasks using Round-Robin scheduling. Automatically handles worker failure with automated dead task reassignment.

S5.title: Scraper Workers
S5.description: Autonomous, containerized worker processes scraping external targets independently. Writes parsed datasets directly into Redis.

S6.title: Caching & Result Buffer
S6.description: High-speed in-memory store buffering intermediate scraping payloads from workers, guaranteeing zero data loss even if the primary orchestrator restarts.

S7.title: Project Related Data Store
S7.description: Document database storing normalized scraping results. Exclusively accessible via the backend orchestrator to isolate schemas and internal APIs from exposure to frontend or worker processes.

H1.title: Fault-Tolerant Queueing
H1.description: RabbitMQ Round-Robin dispatch with worker dead-letter retries. Scraper crashes do not impact cluster stability; dropped tasks automatically re-enqueue.

H2.title: Zero-Data-Loss In-Memory Buffer
H2.description: Redis staging ensures decoupled durability between asynchronous scraping bursts and backend ingestion.

H3.title: Isolated Multi-Tenant Identity
H3.description: Independent ASP.NET Core auth provider with JWT validation, ready for plug-and-play reuse across future services while keeping user credentials fully sandboxed in MS SQL.

H4.title: Horizontal Worker Scalability
H4.description: Dockerized Node.js scraper fleet capable of spinning up dozens of replicas with requests rate limitations to guarantee ethical, continuous store price indexing.
